::: {.decision}
**Your decision.** The importer financed its baseline US$1 million invoice with a dollar loan. At maturity it has the US$300,000 customer receipt and HK$2 million in unrestricted cash. How much of the loan must its bank renew?
:::

## How much principal can treasury repay today?

Assume interest has already been paid. A renewed dollar of principal removes one dollar from the amount due today and creates a future obligation. At 7.80, HK$2 million buys US$256,410. Together with receipts, this covers US$556,410. Minimum rollover is approximately **US$443,590**.

If the bank renews 500,000, the importer buys 200,000 dollars and spends HK$1.56 million. With renewal cut to 400,000 and spot at 7.85, it must buy 300,000 dollars for HK$2.355 million. The cash deficit is **HK$355,000**. This is a funding stress scenario, independent of whether the business will eventually collect additional revenue.

## Can a forward close the funding gap?


```{=html}
<figure class="ess-figure" data-essentials-figure="rollover-gap">
<figcaption><strong>Read the cash shortfall at maturity</strong></figcaption><p>Above zero, the importer needs additional HK-dollar funding. Below zero, it has cash left after repayment. Each line holds the exchange quote fixed.</p>
<div class="ess-chart"></div>
<p><strong>Read the graph.</strong> At renewal of US$400,000, how much would the forward reduce the shortfall?</p>
<details><summary>Check your reading</summary><p>It reduces the gap from HK$355,000 at 7.85 to HK$343,000 at 7.81. Treasury still needs HK$343,000 by maturity.</p></details>
</figure>
```


**Would a forward at 7.81 for the required US$300,000 eliminate the deficit in the stressed scenario?**

<details><summary>Work through the decision</summary><p>It fixes the HK-dollar payment at 2.343 million, leaving a deficit of 343,000. Treasury must also arrange funding or accelerate collections. A foreign lender cutting exposure can transmit a broader capital outflow into a single firm’s maturity schedule. To interpret a country’s aggregate flow, distinguish repayment of old claims from issuance of new ones.</p></details>


```{=html}
<section aria-label="Practice brief"><h2>What must treasury arrange before the dollar loan matures?</h2><details><summary>Compare your recommendation</summary><p>With renewal cut to US$400,000, treasury still needs to buy US$300,000. At 7.85 it lacks HK$355,000. Secure funding or accelerate collections. Locking in 7.81 would still leave a HK$343,000 shortfall.</p></details></section>
```

<details class="full-course-detail"><summary>Turn a Hong Kong dollar funding line into a rollover target</summary><p>A committed HK$200,000 line increases available HK-dollar cash from HK$2 million to HK$2.2 million. At 7.85 that buys about US$280,255. With the US$300,000 receipt, minimum renewal falls to about US$419,745. Confirm the line can be drawn at maturity and include any fees and interest in the subsequent funding schedule.</p></details>
